newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 CEO says undecided on next move in bid.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 CEO says undecided on next move in bid.

text.p: Greg Noval, chief executive of Canadian 88 Energy Corp, said on Thursday he had yet to decide on his mext move after a surprise decision by securities regulators to cease trade of shares in connection with his firm's takeover bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd.
"We may have no choice but to extend our offer now," Noval said in a phone interview. He had said several times during the heated takeover battle he would not extend the C$652-million offer.
The bid was to have expired on Friday.
"We intended to go to the hearing and it's absolutely shocking that they would put it on Monday," Noval said. "I don't know what we're going to do -- our lawyers are in the boardroom as we speak."

The hearing was expected to probe whether Canadian 88's relationship with West Central, a private firm associated with the Calgary-based energy company, should have been more fully disclosed in the takeover circular for Morrison shareholders.

The OSC was also expected to determine whether all Morrison stockholders should be given the opportunity to sell their shares to Canadian 88 on at least the same cash terms as those afforded to West Central prior to the bid being announced.
Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash -- up to a maximum cash portion of C$140 million -- or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
